name: Gmail
blurb: Read, send and draft email for your users
headline: Start today. Going live depends on whether your agent reads email.

firstTest.text: About 20 minutes to a working sign-in with your own app.

production.text: Sending email takes about 1-2 weeks. Reading email takes several weeks to a few months.

approvalWait.text: A scope review usually takes 3-5 business days. Restricted scopes add a yearly security assessment.

whoCanRegister.text: Any Google account can create the app. To go live you need a verified domain, a homepage and a privacy policy.

testMode.text: Testing needs no verification. Only test users you add can sign in, up to 100 over the app's lifetime. Refresh tokens expire after 7 days.

actions.label: Send email
actions.review: Brand check, scope review and a demo video

actions.label: Read email
actions.review: Full verification plus a yearly security assessment (CASA)

steps.title: Book a security assessment lab
steps.detail: Do this only if your agent reads email. It is the slowest step, so start on day one.

steps.title: Create a Google Cloud project
steps.detail: Go to console.cloud.google.com and click New project. Keep it separate from your other work.

steps.title: Set up the consent screen
steps.detail: Open Google Auth Platform and click Get started. Enter the app name, support email, External audience and contact email, then agree to the User Data Policy.

steps.title: Add Gmail permissions
steps.detail: Open Data Access, then Add or remove scopes. Gmail scopes only appear once the Gmail API is enabled; pasting the scope address also works.

steps.title: Add your pilot users
steps.detail: Open Audience, then Test users. Anyone not on the list is blocked with Error 403.

steps.title: Create the OAuth client
steps.detail: Open Clients, pick Web application and add your callback address. Google shows the secret once, so store it in your hosting settings.

steps.title: Prepare brand verification
steps.detail: Verify your domain in Search Console. Publish a homepage and a privacy policy on it, then add both on the Branding page.

steps.title: Write scope justifications
steps.detail: Write one sentence per scope explaining why a narrower scope won't work.

steps.title: Record the demo video
steps.detail: Show the sign-in and every scope in use, with the client ID visible in the address bar.

steps.title: Submit for verification
steps.detail: Open Verification Center and click Prepare for verification. Answer reviewer emails promptly.

blockers.title: Users click 'Back to safety'
blockers.fix: Google highlights Back to safety on the unverified-app warning. Tell pilot users to click Continue.

blockers.title: Pilot users lose access after a week
blockers.fix: Refresh tokens expire after 7 days in testing. Plan for reconnects, or finish verification first.

blockers.title: Users untick a permission
blockers.fix: Google shows one checkbox per permission. Check which scopes came back, and ask again for any that are missing.

blockers.title: You can't verify your callback domain
blockers.fix: Redirect domains become authorized domains. Use a callback on your own verified domain.

blockers.title: Your scope justification reads as vague
blockers.fix: Name the feature that needs each scope, and say why a narrower scope fails.

agentCan: Fill in the consent screen and scope forms from your product details
Draft scope justifications and the demo video script
Check your site for a privacy policy and homepage before you submit
youDo: Sign in to Google Cloud and agree to Google's policies
Verify your domain (DNS or Search Console)
Store the client secret in your hosting settings
Pay for the security assessment and complete it

drafts.title: Justification for sending email
drafts.body: Our assistant sends replies that the user has reviewed and approved in our app. gmail.send is the narrowest scope that allows sending; we do not read, modify or delete existing mail.

drafts.title: Justification for reading email
drafts.body: Our assistant summarises the user's support inbox so they can triage faster. It needs message bodies, which gmail.metadata does not include. We never modify or delete mail.

drafts.title: Demo video script
drafts.body:
1. Show the app homepage and privacy policy link.
2. Click Connect Gmail; show the consent screen with the client ID in the address bar.
3. Show each permission in use: a summary (read) and a sent reply (send).
4. Show how a user disconnects.
